about.about: Equinox is a game streaming client for the Nintendo Switch, built to pair with the Solstice host. It also works with Sunshine.
about.thanks_1:  Rock88 and his Moonlight-NX, lots of code was reused in this app
about.thanks_3:  Moonlight team, it could not be possible without them
about.thanks_4:  Cameron Gutman for helping to solve an issue with LibNX
about.title: About
about.fork_text: Equinox is an unofficial fork of Moonlight-Switch by XITRIX. Most of the streaming client comes from that project and from Moonlight. Equinox is not affiliated with or endorsed by their authors.
about.support_text: Equinox is free. If it helps you, you can buy the developer a coffee: point your phone camera at the code or open the link.

info.frame_pacing:
Sets how many frames are held before they reach the screen.

Lowest latency shows each frame as soon as it arrives: controls feel faster, but the picture can hitch if the network wobbles.

Smoothest video keeps a few frames in reserve: motion is more fluid, with a little more delay. Balanced sits in between.
info.resolution_scale:
Only applies when the resolution is set to Native. It multiplies the screen size used for the stream.

0.5x and 0.75x are lighter on the network and the device. 2.0x asks for a picture larger than the screen: sharper, but much heavier.
info.codec:
The format the PC uses to compress the video before sending it.

H.264 works everywhere. HEVC (H.265) gives the same quality with less bitrate, which helps on Wi-Fi. AV1 is the most efficient but needs a recent graphics card in the PC.

If the picture breaks up or the stream won't start, go back to H.264.
info.decoder:
How many processor cores help decode the video.

More threads help at high resolutions but use more CPU. If unsure, keep the default.
info.use_hw_decoding: Uses the device's video chip to decode the stream instead of the processor. Everything runs lighter and with less delay.
info.bitrate:
How much data the PC sends each second.

A higher bitrate gives a cleaner picture, especially in fast scenes, but needs a better network. If the stream stutters or drops frames, lower it.

The recommended minimum for your resolution and FPS is shown next to the title.
info.dithering:
Adds a very fine noise over the picture to hide color banding, common in skies and dark gradients.

The slider sets the strength.
info.upscaling: When the stream arrives at a lower resolution than the screen, AMD FSR enlarges it with sharper edges instead of just stretching it.
info.rcas:
Brings out edges and textures so the picture looks sharper.

Too much can make edges jagged. The slider sets the strength.
info.show_metrics:
Shows a summary of how the stream is doing in a corner of the screen while you play:

FPS: frames shown per second.
ms: estimated delay between the PC and your screen.
Mbps: how much video is actually arriving.
Loss: frames lost on the network. Turns orange from 1% and red from 5%.
